# id: # evalorder/unseq-addr — Stage E5 family E5d (evaluation-order model v2.1 §7 row E; lane
# core/unseq-stage-e5-0922, 2026-09-22): the ADDRESS of a variable as an operand — an address formation (no read,
# no failure), NO occurrence of the graph; the reads of the address-taken variable beside the receiving call are.
# Each membership row's sweep lowers as ONE `unseq` graph; the ONE consumption site is the `unseq` scheduler's
# pick (`unseqNext`, bound = the ready-set size). The strict row is the control.

subject: addrArgVsRead
why: E5d1 `use(&x) + x`: use writes *p = 7 and returns 1; &x is an address formation carried as the argument `ref x` (no read); the sibling read of the address-taken x is spec-unsequenced against use — before 1 + 1 = 2, after 7 + 1 = 8; the ONE consumption site is the `unseq` scheduler's pick (`unseqNext`, bound = the ready-set size at each pick; Stage E5 E5d, 2026-09-22 — design docs/2026-09-22_unseq-stage-e5-design.md §E5d). members=2

subject: addrPayloadVsCall
why: E5d2 `*(&PT{p: &x}).p + m()`: m writes x = 10 and returns 5; &x is the struct literal's payload `ref x` (no read), the literal an allocate body without an E1 edge (ratified item 6); the dereference through the fresh pointer's field reads x, spec-unsequenced against m — before 1 + 5 = 6, after 10 + 5 = 15; the ONE consumption site is the `unseq` scheduler's pick (`unseqNext`, bound = the ready-set size at each pick; Stage E5 E5d, 2026-09-22 — design docs/2026-09-22_unseq-stage-e5-design.md §E5d). members=2

subject: addrStoredVsRead
why: E5d3 `p, y = &x, use(&x)+x; *p*10 + y`: a tuple with no planned target — the stored address rides the completion (no occurrence); y's sweep is E5d1's (x's read vs use): 2 or 8; *p reads x = 7 after the sweep — 72 or 78; the ONE consumption site is the `unseq` scheduler's pick (`unseqNext`, bound = the ready-set size at each pick; Stage E5 E5d, 2026-09-22 — design docs/2026-09-22_unseq-stage-e5-design.md §E5d). members=2

subject: addrGlobalArgVsRead
why: E5d1 (package-level) `use(&g) + g`: &g is the seeded cell's address (`globaladdr`, no read); g's read is a `deref(globaladdr)` occurrence (E1) spec-unsequenced against use writing *p = 7 — before 1 + 1 = 2, after 7 + 1 = 8; the ONE consumption site is the `unseq` scheduler's pick (`unseqNext`, bound = the ready-set size at each pick; Stage E5 E5d, 2026-09-22 — design docs/2026-09-22_unseq-stage-e5-design.md §E5d). members=2
